scope: complete repository, weighted toward surfaces changed by cross-cutting PRs #103, #112, #117, #119, #122
dimensions: duplicated semantics and coupling; dead paths and obsolete compatibility; hot files, hidden state, config and naming; test seams and CI execution honesty
verdict: Core seams (single RPC transport, contract routes, smoke/live selection, loud-skip tests) are well designed but each has 1-2 uncontrolled bypasses accumulating; two high-churn shared files are re-growing the exact collision pattern that caused prior regressions.

findings.impact: .env.example still calls the adapter defaults 'non-functional placeholders', but PR #112 made the real deployed Base adapter addresses the config defaults; an operator following the file believes vault-economics is broken or pastes stale addresses over correct defaults.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the .env.example adapter block: defaults are the live Base mainnet adapter addresses; override only for a re-pointed deployment (mirror the config.ts:50 comment).

findings.impact: Regime classification thresholds are implemented three times and have already diverged: the canonical classifier uses 0.33/0.67 while committee domain.ts and mcp memo.ts use 0.45/0.55 — a composite of 0.60 is 'neutral' to the classifier but 'risk_on' to the committee layer. backfillRegimeHistory additionally inserts synthetic rows labeled with the divergent rule into the classifier-owned regime_snapshots table on the live aggregation path, so one table can mix two classification semantics; any threshold retune is a three-site hunt.
findings.recommendation: Export the classifier thresholds/label function from one module (analytics/analyze/regime.ts or contract) and consume it in committee/domain.ts and mcp/src/memo.ts; make backfill/summary read stored labels only, never re-derive with a local rule.

findings.impact: What counts as a transient HTTP failure is re-derived per fetcher with divergent rules: base-rpc-client retries {429,502,503,504} honoring Retry-After; edgar.ts retries all 5xx with a fixed ladder and ignores Retry-After; the shared extract/http.ts (FRED/Yahoo/DefiLlama/GeckoTerminal) has no retry at all. A rate-limit-handling improvement like #119's must be re-implemented per fetcher instead of landing once in the shared seam.
findings.recommendation: Add optional bounded retry (shared transient-status set + Retry-After parsing, both already written in base-rpc-client) to extract/http.ts and let edgar/live-source/token-prices opt in; keep worker-loop backoff separate.

findings.impact: Every consumer suite of the RPC transport monkey-patches globalThis.fetch and must remember to restore it and reset the module-level semaphore; safe under bun's sequential per-file execution but order-coupled if test parallelism ever changes.
findings.recommendation: No action required now; if a third suite grows around this transport, add a shared with-mocked-rpc helper in backend/tests/support/ that installs/restores fetch and resets the gate.

findings.impact: Backoff uses real setTimeout + Math.random jitter with no injectable sleep/clock; tests compensate by shrinking real waits via env knobs (BASE_RPC_RETRY_BASE_MS=1) or steering around sleeps with non-retryable status codes. The 50ms-vs-60ms timeout-race test is coupled to wall-clock scheduling and can flake on a loaded CI runner; every new retry surface must re-invent the workaround.
findings.recommendation: Accept an optional injected sleep/now (defaulting to real) in RpcCallOptions or via a module test hook, and use it in edgar.ts's retry loop, so retry-timing tests become virtual-time and deterministic.

findings.impact: Six chain modules hand-copy the identical 'CACHE_TTL_MS = 30_000; let cache; _resetXForTests()' in-process cache pattern; a cache-policy change (TTL jitter, invalidation when BASE_RPC_SOURCE flips) is a six-file edit and each module hand-writes its own test-reset hook.
findings.recommendation: One ttlCached(fn, ttl) helper in chain/ with a bypass option and a shared test-reset registry; replace the six copies.

findings.impact: Per-asset valuation semantics (valuationKind switch, strategy-NAV-in-6dp-USDC rule, provenance ternary) are copied between wallet-balances and wallet-sleeves, and divergence has started: #119 rewrote wallet-balances to batched Multicall3 and deleted readAmount(), but wallet-sleeves.ts:82 still says 'Mirrors wallet-balances.ts::readAmount' (a function that no longer exists) and still fans out unbatched per-request eth_calls. The next valuationKind or provenance change is a silent two-site edit.
findings.recommendation: Extract one shared per-asset valuation module (kind-to-amount decode, decimals, provenance rules) that both endpoints call, and batch sleeves' reads through the same Multicall3 helper keyed per wallet.

findings.impact: Four smoke/committee business values are maintained as comment-enforced mirrors across packages with no compile or test guard: COMMITTEE_ROSTER_CAP=10, the NO_SHOWS/attends() rule, the stanceFor() threshold ladder (byte-identical in backend smoke/e2e.ts and mcp/agent.ts), and the four-member roster. mcp already depends on @robotmoney/contract — the sanctioned cross-boundary channel — so the 'mcp can't import backend' rationale does not hold; changing the cap or ladder in one package silently desynchronizes smoke onboarding from the backend gate.
findings.recommendation: Move the shared smoke constants (roster cap, roster, no-show rule, stance thresholds) into @robotmoney/contract or a shared smoke-fixtures module imported by backend, mcp, and scripts; delete the mirrors.

findings.impact: Demo fixture generation (hardcoded WOON/MAV baskets, ensureSmokeSubjectFixtures, synthetic regime backfill) lives inside the production committee domain module, and the live aggregateSession path unconditionally runs backfillRegimeHistory — a sparse real deployment gets synthetic rows written into regime_snapshots indistinguishable from classifier output. Templated synthesis prose hardcodes the '95/5/0/0' mandate as string literals even though the weights are admin-editable via allocation_framework; an admin rebalance leaves every future session narrating stale policy. Wiring real inference (#77) requires surgically separating the rollup from ~80 lines of interleaved template text.
findings.recommendation: Move fixture seeding and regime backfill behind an explicit smoke-only module/flag (never on the unconditional live aggregation path); derive mandate numbers from getAllocationFramework(); keep aggregateSession's rollup math separate from narrative enrichment so the inference seam is one function.

findings.impact: config.ts opens with 'Central environment configuration' but ~20 backend knobs are read deep in call stacks and ~56 of 66 total env vars are absent from .env.example. Operators of the two deploy targets (hermetic smoke compose vs the tunnel host) cannot discover knobs like BUYBACK_LOG_CHUNK or FETCH_CACHE_TTL_MS without grepping source, so deployments drift and incident fixes get applied to one target only. The call-time-read pattern itself is deliberate (testability); the problem is discoverability.
findings.recommendation: Route every backend env read through named resolver functions in config.ts (the resolveX(env) pattern already exists), regenerate .env.example or a docs/configuration table enumerating all knobs with defaults, and add a CI grep failing new process.env reads in backend/src outside config.ts.

findings.impact: The retired PROVIDER knob survives as a dead chain: config.analyticsProvider is computed from process.env.PROVIDER but has zero consumers; fetcher-provider.ts (63 lines of self-described test-only scaffolding in src/) is imported only by tests, carries comments referencing a deleted access/select.ts, and pins a back-compat loadSources export in extract/sources.ts. Meanwhile committee.ts's unrelated analyticsProvider() auth predicate collides with the name — a developer grepping to change the data source lands in the auth path, and setting PROVIDER=live changes no behavior.
findings.recommendation: Delete config.analyticsProvider and the PROVIDER env read (migrate the retired test scaffolding); move fetcher-provider.ts under backend/tests/ or delete it with providers.test.ts; inline loadSources; rename the committee.ts predicate to hasAnalyticsRole().

findings.impact: Config values exist both as frozen load-time snapshots (config.propWallets etc.) and call-time resolvers (resolvePropWallets(env)); modules using different access paths can disagree when env flips (mainly tests today), making 'which value am I seeing' a per-call investigation. blockDateCache in buyback-logs is invisible cross-request state that never invalidates on reorg.
findings.recommendation: Pick one access pattern per value — resolver or snapshot — and remove the duplicate; note a size cap/reorg policy on blockDateCache while touching buyback-logs for the tracked reorg-margin follow-up.

findings.impact: The one-shot importer that upserts the vendored 2026-06-25 regime fixture into regime_snapshots has zero callers and predates #112's no-baked-data-on-live-path posture; an operator debugging the known stale-/regime-charts symptom who finds it can overwrite live pipeline snapshots with June fixture data in prod. The mapper and .gz fixture it shares are live (Playwright stubs) — only the DB importer is orphaned.
findings.recommendation: Delete backend/src/db/import-regime-eq.ts (Playwright specs consume the mapper directly), or gate it behind RM_ENV!=prod with a loud warning.

findings.impact: The backend base URL is configured as API_BASE in one driver and BACKEND_URL in five others; exporting BACKEND_URL silently fails to repoint backend/src/smoke/e2e.ts, which falls back to localhost:8787 — a confusing partial-override failure mode rmpc-release-e2e.ts already hand-compensates for.
findings.recommendation: Rename API_BASE to BACKEND_URL in backend/src/smoke/e2e.ts (accept the old name for one release if needed) so every driver honors one variable.

findings.impact: base-rpc-client.ts declares itself the single JSON-RPC transport for every Base read ('do NOT hand-roll a fetch to the RPC elsewhere' — the #112/#119 invariant), yet projects/access/live-source.ts hand-rolls its own eth_call fetch with a duplicate selector table. The bypass gets none of the #119 rate-limit controls: no concurrency-gate participation, no 429/Retry-After retry, no User-Agent (the public Base node 403s bare POSTs per the client's own comment), different timeout mechanism. The live vault-TVL cron shares the same public RPC as wallet sampling, so every future rate-limit fix must be re-implemented here — the invariant has already diverged once.
findings.recommendation: Route live-source's ethCall through chain/base-rpc-client (add asset()/decimals() selector helpers there) and delete the local SEL table and hand-rolled fetch.

findings.impact: PROJECTS_SOURCE is required in prod (select.ts throws 'projects pipelines require PROJECTS_SOURCE=live in prod') yet is set or documented nowhere an operator looks — zero hits across docs/, .env.example, README, compose files, .github/. The seven projects.* cron schedules are seeded enabled by default, so a prod deployment following the shipped compose/env files has its projects pipelines crash-loop on an undiscoverable env var; every other operative knob IS in .env.example, so its absence reads as 'no such knob'.
findings.recommendation: Add PROJECTS_SOURCE to .env.example (commented, with the prod-requires-live fail-closed semantics) and to the compose env passthrough alongside ANALYTICS_SOURCE; mention it in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.

findings.impact: The nightly live-fetchers job has no execution-evidence guard: if the RUN_LIVE_FETCHERS gate name ever drifts between workflow and test files, every live test becomes test.skip, the fallback 'gate is documented' test passes, bun exits 0, and the nightly stays green while validating zero live endpoints — the false-green the repo's policy item 2 forbids. Wiring is correct today; this is a latent guard-rail gap.
findings.recommendation: Have the nightly set EXPECT_LIVE=1 and make each fallback test fail under EXPECT_LIVE when the gate is off, or grep the bun test summary in the workflow and fail on zero passes / any skips.

findings.impact: projects-fetchers-live.test.ts deviates from the repo's own live-suite convention: run with the gate off it collects only skipped tests and exits 0 with zero executed assertions, while the three sibling live suites each register a fallback assertion. Inconsistency erodes the convention for future live suites.
findings.recommendation: Add the same !LIVE fallback test the other three live suites carry, keeping every file's exit-0 backed by at least one executed assertion.

findings.impact: routes.js is documented as the single source of truth for URLs, but the committee surface bypasses it in both directions: ROUTES.committee omits the live endpoints (open-session, signing-payload, memos, verify-token, register, regime, admin/*), and backend committee.ts plus mcp/src/e2e.ts (~20 sites) plus two scripts hardcode the paths as string literals. check-contract CI only diffs the vendored frontend copy, so none of this drift is caught; a committee endpoint rename is a manual chase across four packages and the contract no longer describes the real API.
findings.recommendation: Complete ROUTES.committee (+admin lifecycle) in contract/src/routes.js and consume it in backend committee.ts, mcp/src/e2e.ts, and the scripts; add a test asserting every registered /api/ path appears in ROUTES.

findings.impact: The 463-line audit still states '4/25 pages complete (16%)' and 'Ready for Phase 0 kickoff' and lists shipped views (smart-contract-risks, tech-proposal-march-16, regime_2panel) as dropped scope, though the port phase is complete on main; it also pins a personal branch/worktree path. docs/screenshots/README.md points readers at it as current and instructs starting a legacy dev server. Anyone triaging docs concludes 21 pages of work remain and may re-plan completed work.
findings.recommendation: Delete docs/FEATURE_PARITY_PLAN.md (plan-tracking lives in the GitHub Plan issue) or prepend a COMPLETED banner with closing PR references; fix docs/screenshots/README.md in the same pass.

findings.impact: The plan shipped in the same commit that last touched it (PR #34) but carries no status marker: Phases 4-5 read as pending work and it asserts stale facts ('feat/12 is a bare worktree today'). Readers cannot tell executed design record from open plan, and it is the only doc trail for import-regime-eq.ts.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Status: COMPLETED via PR #34; retained as design record' header, or fold the still-true facts into ARCHITECTURE.md and delete the plan.

findings.impact: Three doc-filename schemes (SCREAMING, SCREAMING_SNAKE, Caps-Dash) coexist with the decided kebab-case convention, so links and grep patterns to canonical docs keep breaking as files get renamed piecemeal. Known drift, already tracked under issue #113; recorded here for completeness.
findings.recommendation: Batch-rename to kebab-case with a link-fixing pass in one PR per the 2026-07-10 convention decision.

findings.impact: The same-selector duplicate-block pattern that caused the #80 committee layout regression has re-accumulated: two base blocks and two @media(min-width:768px) blocks both style .cv__context-grid/.cv__discussion/.cv__portfolio-grid with different values (line 310 sets repeat(2,...) which line 346 overrides to 0.75fr 1.25fr). The later block silently wins, so editing the first is a no-op and a merge that reorders or drops one block changes layout with no diff noise; 13 commits since May make that merge scenario likely.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate each selector to one base block and one @media(min-width:768px) block; add a cheap CI lint failing duplicate top-level selector groups within the same media context, since this is the second recurrence.

findings.impact: Committee entities exist in two casing dialects (snake_case archive JSON and regime_summary inner keys vs camelCase API DTOs), reconciled by hand-written frontend normalizers (camelSession/camelTake/camelMember/normalizeSnapshot) on top of the backend's own row-to-DTO mapper — the same field mapping implemented repeatedly. This exact seam already produced the subject_id/subjectId archive render bug. Load-bearing shapes (regimeSummary, committeeRecommendation) are typed `unknown` in contract/src/committee.d.ts so nothing catches drift before render time, and `||` coalescing silently drops legitimate 0/empty-string/false values.
findings.recommendation: Type RegimeSummary and CommitteeRecommendation in contract (declaring the canonical casing), keep a single shared normalizer module, and replace `||` with `??` for value fields.

findings.impact: Twelve unrelated page views (regime, allocation, committee, admin jobs, comments, buyback, projects...) share one 1350-line file that nearly every recent PR (#112, #117, #119, #122) edited — the highest-churn code file in the repo (20 commits since May). This is the same shared-file collision pattern that produced the views.css regression (#80): concurrent PRs merge textually clean but semantically collide, and a bad merge in one view silently breaks another.
findings.recommendation: Split into one module per Alpine factory (alpine/views/regime.js, allocation.js, admin-jobs.js, ...) with a thin registerViews(Alpine) barrel; the boot-time registration constraint (views inject via innerHTML) is unaffected.

findings.impact: committee-controllers.js and committee-archive.js (166 lines shipped to browsers) are unreachable in production: index.html loads only main.js, whose import graph never includes them, and their sole referencer is scripts/tests/frontend-routes.test.ts. They were dev-scout stubs (#46) superseded by static-views.js, which reimplements the same archive loading and snake-to-camel normalization. Consequence: the '/committee/... controller resolves static archive data' test passes green while exercising code no browser runs — false coverage for the real archive path — and two divergent normalizers invite the exact drift class that caused the subject_id/subjectId render bug.
findings.recommendation: Delete committee-controllers.js and committee-archive.js; rewrite the archive-resolution test against the loaders static-views.js actually uses (export them or extract a shared lib both import).

findings.impact: The stance vocabulary (bullish/constructive/neutral/cautious/bearish) is independently declared in mcp, backend domain, and twice in the frontend as identical inline hex color maps, while contract types stance as plain string. Adding or renaming a stance touches 5+ files in three packages, and the two frontend color maps can diverge silently today.
findings.recommendation: Declare the stance enum + canonical order in contract; derive both frontend color maps from one shared map keyed by that enum.

findings.impact: The three most-edited behavioral units in the churned areas are far past the ~80-line threshold with dense branching: regimeView (~262 lines, 62 branch tokens), allocationView (~225 lines), aggregateSession (~112 lines in a 619-line file mixing persistence, basket simulation, brief templating, and regime-summary building). Fixes to one branch require re-understanding the whole function, and the recent casing/render bugs clustered exactly here.
findings.recommendation: Decompose regimeView and allocationView into pure chart-data helpers (the alignToDates pattern already exists) unit-testable outside Alpine; split aggregateSession's templating and regime-summary steps into named functions in separate modules.

findings.impact: Provenance comments claim page numbers are baked or 'computed at render time' from data files (public/data/weighting-comparison.json, regime-snapshot.json, src/data/changelog.ts) that do not exist in this repo — they are legacy robotmoney-site paths. Post-#112, these comments are the only provenance the static pages have, so wrong pointers actively rot; a maintainer refreshing a figure follows them to nothing.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite each provenance comment to name the real source, e.g. 'numbers frozen from robotmoney-site public/data/... as of <date>' or the live API route that now owns the number.

findings.impact: 27 MB / 33 full-page PNGs of the original Next.js site are committed as 'visual parity fixtures' with zero programmatic consumers — the visual spec gates on its own separately committed Playwright baselines. With the port phase complete these are frozen artifacts of a finished one-time review: they bloat every clone by 27 MB and imply an ongoing screenshot-parity process that does not exist. Deletion needs owner confirmation that the manual parity review is closed.
findings.recommendation: Delete frontend/test/fixtures/screenshots/original/ (keep the Playwright *-snapshots baselines) or move the captures to an issue/release attachment; update the fixtures README and spec comment.

findings.impact: RM_ALLOW_INSECURE has opposite default polarity in its two readers: the backend treats unset as secure (insecure only on explicit ==="1" opt-in), the e2e driver treats unset as insecure (opt-out via ==="0"). Anyone copying the e2e idiom into new backend/script code inverts a security default; anyone setting RM_ALLOW_INSECURE=0 believing it hardens the backend changes only the e2e path. Divergent semantics for one flag name is how a fail-open regression slips through review.
findings.recommendation: Make mcp/src/e2e.ts use the same opt-in convention (==="1") or derive its expectation from RM_ENV like the backend; document the flag's single contract in one place referenced by both readers.

findings.impact: smoke-main.ts (1131 lines, >=9 concerns: port allocation, TUI state machine, console patching, compose lifecycle, readiness probes, polling, onboarding) is edited by every feature adding a smoke-visible surface (5 distinct feature PRs; the churn from the former #1-churn smoke.ts moved here). Concerns interleave through module-level mutable state, and line 113 mutates process.env.ADMIN_TOKEN globally, making section ordering load-bearing; concurrent smoke-touching PRs collide.
findings.recommendation: Extract independent concerns into scripts/lib modules (tui-state, compose, readiness, research-poll) with explicit state passed in, leaving smoke-main.ts as orchestration; pass the admin token explicitly instead of mutating process.env.

findings.impact: The CI goldens drift gate is specified (preview-server-spec §5) but not wired, while scripts/update-goldens.ts's header claims the opposite ('a CI drift gate blocks a PR whose goldens no longer match the code'). A backend shape change can merge with stale goldens: the Playwright suite stubs routes FROM the goldens so it keeps passing against the old shape, and the preview server then replays a contract that no longer exists. The hermetic e2e partially mitigates; the misleading comment actively tells readers the gap is closed.
findings.recommendation: Wire the spec's option B (hermetic per-PR gate validating goldens against contract types and the frontend route set), or at minimum correct the update-goldens.ts header to say specified-but-unwired.

clean_areas: Multicall3 + 429 retry test coverage (backend/tests/base-rpc-client.test.ts): retry, Retry-After, exhausted-retries-still-throws, concurrency cap, timeout bound, and the twelve-reads-to-one-eth_call property all executed against the real transport with fetch mocked only at the process boundary
Wallet-balances path tests drive the real multicall batch through the real rpcRequest against ephemeral Postgres, including per-leg degradation and the config collision guard asserted both ways
Committee inference bounding (mcp/tests/inference.test.ts): injectable OPENCODE_BIN/OPENCODE_TIMEOUT_MS seams; loud-skip contract and grandchild-keeps-pipes-open timeout proven hermetically

DB loud-skip: backend/bunfig.toml preload throws when Docker/Postgres is absent — integration suite goes red, never green-via-skip; CI executes tests for every surface (root, backend, mcp, Playwright, smoke-frontend-check + live-leak guard)
Frontend-to-backend URL contract for browser code: zero hardcoded /api/ paths outside the vendored contract copy, which is byte-identical to contract/src/routes.js and CI-guarded
No api-to-smoke dependency: backend/src/api never imports backend/src/smoke; the only smoke import from prod code is flag-gated seeding
Projects smoke/live seam is a proper interface (ProjectsDataSource with fail-closed selection; transforms.ts single pure implementation shared by worker and fidelity suite)
Committee cryptographic canonicalization single-sourced in @robotmoney/contract and imported by backend, mcp, and the smoke driver
chain layer pricing/decoding genuinely shared (buyback-logs, token-metrics, vault-economics, wallet-* all consume base-rpc-client + token-prices)

scripts/smoke.ts reduced to a 12-line shim (the extraction was right; residual concern is smoke-main.ts, finding 032); smoke/hermetic flag layering in scripts/lib/smoke-env.ts coherent, single-sourced, and tested
COMMITTEE_REAL_INFERENCE read only at its two entry points with consistent semantics; heroes.js is large but single-concern with independent factories

goldens/api-goldens.json route keys match the live API surface; all package.json scripts resolve; compose env keys all have readers; SPA views all reachable via router catch-all plus in-page links; frontend/public/data/committee/** is live (static-views.js archive path), not #112 leftovers
unresolved_decisions: Whether frontend/test/fixtures/screenshots/original/ (27 MB) may be deleted — README documents intended manual-review use; needs owner confirmation the one-time parity review is closed (finding 030)
Whether the seeded-degradation provider seam (fetcher-provider.ts + providers.test.ts) is still a contract worth keeping in tests/ or should be deleted outright (finding 011)
limitations: Static review at pinned commit 4fc1236; no test suite was executed (backend preload provisions Docker Postgres — outside the review budget), so bun exit-0-on-all-skipped behavior is asserted from bun semantics, not observed
Branch-protection required-status-check list not visible in the repo; language-coverage of required checks inferred from workflow design
Env-var inventory was regex-based (process.env.X / Bun.env.X); vars read via destructured env objects may be missed

No whole-backend per-export dead-code sweep (no ts-prune); dead-path findings cover the #112 blast radius, flags, docs, and scripts specifically
Churn window measured from 2026-05-01; earlier history may shift hot-file ranking
